messages:
Jia: heads-up — canary qwen2.5 serving shows a ~18% p95 latency bump after last night's kernel-selector tweak, started at ~01:20 UTC in us-west-2 :eyes:

Mike: can you paste the profiling/kern-choser logs? I saw tail noise earlier but not sure it was related.

Jia: dropping snippets. kernel-selector now prefers "sparse_fused_v3" for many layers; KV cache hit_rate collapses and batching tail grows.

Jia: ```
[2026-03-18T01:19:58Z] kernel-choice: selected "sparse_fused_v3" (score=0.81)
[2026-03-18T01:20:01Z] batch-sampler: batch_target=6 observed_avg=4 latency_ms=24 p95=165
[2026-03-18T01:20:03Z] kv-cache: hit_rate=0.66 -> 0.33 (reqs/s=910)
[2026-03-18T01:20:05Z] tokenizer: lang=ja input_len=52 subtokens=68 -> boundary_shift=1
```

Sara: that tokenizer line jumps out. In my local runs with mixed ja/en prompts I see subtoken boundaries flipping if punctuation differs — our CJK fallback is non-deterministic in edge cases.

Oliver: if tokenization changes, prefix-KV keys differ -> cache misses -> more KV repopulation -> higher per-request work. explains tail.

Mike: do we have distribution of KV repop events per request before vs after?

Jia: canary traces:

Jia: ```
kv_population_events_per_request: median=1 mean=1.9 p95=6
baseline p95=2
after change p95=6
```

Sara: also seeing RoPE phase drift in qwen2.5 when token boundaries shift mid-sequence — sparse_fused_v3's cross-request grouping heuristic is batching across tokenization variants and amplifying phase misalignment.

perf-bot: alert: regression_detected(qwen2p5-canary, latency_p95, +18%) — investigate

Oliver: two quick mitigations: (1) rollback the grouping heuristic that widened cross-request batching; (2) normalize punctuation for CJK before tokenization to force deterministic splits; (3) add cheap pre-batch compatibility filter to avoid grouping requests with different tokenization patterns.

Mike: prefer (3) + non-blocking normalization. Rolling back loses perf for standard en workloads. also we should profile interactions with ALiBi fallback vs RoPE scaling options.

Sara: ran an AB on rope params locally. results summary:

Sara: ```
rope_scale=1.00 -> baseline p95
rope_scale=1.04 -> mixed ja/en p95 +5%, KV_hit -8%
rope_decay=0.999 -> p95 +2%, KV_hit -3%
```

Sara: small increases in rope_scale appear to worsen mixed-lang cases because tiny phase shifts accumulate when token boundaries shift across requests.

Jia: noticed kernel mismatch warnings: "kv_dim!=head_dim (48 vs 64)" for some layers — that forces runtime to fall back to generic kernels which are slower and bypass some KV optimizations.

Mike: which converter produced that model? if kv_pack rounded down to 48 while head_dim is 64 that's a bug in conversion. which variant is on canary?

Jia: canary is qwen2.5-16b-convert-v1. conversion log shows `kv_pack: round_to_48` for memory packing; head_dim was 64 for those layers so mismatch happened.

Oliver: that explains kernel flips + tokenizer churn compounding into tail. packed kv with incompatible dims breaks kernel selection heuristics.

Mike: short-term plan: revert the sparse_fused_v3 grouping change (rollback PR) and gate aggressive grouping behind a runtime check (if kv_hit_rate < 0.5 or tokenization_variance > 0.12 then avoid cross-lang grouping). medium-term: fix converter to keep kv_dim == head_dim or add a safe remapping shim in runtime.

Sara: I'll own the mixed-lang perf harness and add it to nightly regression suite; will test tokenizer-normalize and the compatibility pre-filter.

Jia: opening rollback PR now and adding correlation logs to the autokernel ticket. also adding a runtime safety barrier: if tokenizer_lang_mismatch_ratio > 0.1 then prefer conservative grouping.

Mike: assigning myself the converter audit. will add unit tests that assert kv_dim == head_dim and a golden conversion test with ja/zh samples.

perf-bot: deploy-requested(canary-rollback-sparsegroup, by Jia) — queued

Oliver: thanks team. check p95 in ~45m after rollback. nice catch. :clap:

Sara: repro curl for canary with mixed ja/en example:

Sara: ```bash
curl -X POST https://canary.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY" \
  -d '{"model":"qwen2p5","input":"今日の天気はどうですか？ Also, any update on the deployment tomorrow?"}'
```

Jia: keeping thread open until canary stabilizes.
